objectives: Quantify air + water + lead burdens + name key cohort studies.
Connect climate change to health (heat, vectors, food, migration).
Apply Bradford Hill + occupational hierarchy of controls to workplace hazards.

slides.title: Air, water, housing: the classical environmental burden
slides.body:
**Air pollution** — the largest single environmental risk factor; ~7 million deaths/yr globally (WHO 2024; State of Global Air; GBD).

**PM2.5** — fine particulate matter ≤2.5 μm; penetrates alveoli + crosses into bloodstream. Sources: combustion (coal, biomass, diesel, gasoline), industrial, secondary atmospheric formation from SO₂ + NOₓ + VOCs. **Harvard Six Cities Study** (Dockery + Pope 1993 NEJM) — landmark prospective cohort of 8,111 adults across six US cities showed strong + linear relationship between PM2.5 + all-cause + cardiopulmonary + lung-cancer mortality. **Pope + Dockery (1995, 2002 JAMA)** — ACS Cancer Prevention Study II extended the analysis to ~500k adults: each 10 μg/m³ increment in PM2.5 → ~6-10% increase in cardiopulmonary mortality. Foundation of EPA + WHO air-quality regulation.

**WHO Air Quality Guidelines 2021** — annual mean PM2.5 ≤ 5 μg/m³ (previous: 10); 24-hr 15 μg/m³; PM10 15 + 45; NO₂ 10 + 25; O₃ 60 (peak season). Most of the world's population lives in air exceeding 10× the guideline. **Chinese smog**: peak PM2.5 in Beijing 2013 reached >500 μg/m³ ('Airpocalypse'); Action Plan 2013 + Blue Sky 2017 reduced PM2.5 ~40% by 2020 (Geng + Zhang 2021). **India** has some of the worst urban air globally (Delhi 100-300 μg/m³ annual mean; CPCB + Ghude); state-level policy + Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala (LPG access for cooking) target household + ambient sources.

**Ozone (O₃)** — secondary pollutant from VOCs + NOₓ + sunlight. Asthma exacerbation + premature mortality (Bell + Dominici).

**Household air pollution (HAP)** — biomass + coal cookstoves; ~2.3 billion exposed; ~3 million deaths/yr (Smith). Improved cookstoves + transition to LPG / electricity central to PH + climate co-benefits.

**Lead** — neurotoxin; no safe threshold. **Reuben et al. (2017 JAMA + 2019 JAMA Pediatrics)** — Dunedin birth cohort showed childhood lead exposure (median ~10 μg/dL in 1970s NZ) → 4-7 IQ point loss + lifetime SES decline. Tetraethyl lead removed from US gasoline 1996; childhood blood lead dropped from ~16 μg/dL (1976) to ~0.8 (2020) — biggest environmental success. **Flint MI 2014-2015** — switched water source → corrosion → lead in tap water → blood lead doubled (Hanna-Attisha 2016 AJPH). Lead paint banned US 1978 (NL 1973); legacy housing burden remains. WHO lead reference value 5 μg/dL (2010); CDC dropped to 3.5 (2021).

**Cholera + waterborne disease** — Snow 1854 to 2010 Haiti epidemic (UN peacekeepers introduced cholera strain via inadequate sanitation; >800k cases; ~10k deaths; Frerichs). WASH (Water, Sanitation, Hygiene) interventions cut diarrhea ~30-50% (Wolf 2018 Trop Med Int Health meta-analysis). SDG 6 targets universal water + sanitation by 2030; far off-track in LMICs.

**Legionella** — pneumonic + Pontiac fever; cooling towers + plumbing biofilms. American Legion convention Philadelphia 1976 — first identified outbreak (Fraser 1977 NEJM). Aerosols + hot water systems are vectors; routine monitoring + chlorination required.

**Radon** — naturally occurring radioactive gas in soil; second leading cause of lung cancer (after tobacco). EPA action level 4 pCi/L; mitigation via sub-slab depressurization in homes.

**Asbestos** — fibrous silicate; mesothelioma + lung cancer + asbestosis; latency 20-40 yr. Selikoff 1964 — insulation workers cohort established carcinogenicity. Banned EU + Australia; partial bans US (final EPA chrysotile ban 2024). Global toll continues from imports + legacy buildings (UK ~5000 deaths/yr).

**Indoor air + radon + tobacco smoke**: smoking is itself a major indoor air pollutant. Public smoke-free laws (Ireland 2004 first; Helena MT natural experiment) dropped hospital AMIs ~13% (Sargent 2004 BMJ).

**Housing** — overcrowding, mold, cold, lead, vermin; social determinants nexus. WHO Housing + Health Guidelines 2018.

slides.title: Climate change + planetary health
slides.body:
**Climate change** is the defining 21st-century public-health challenge. Pathways from warming to health are direct (heat, weather extremes) + indirect (food, water, vectors, conflict, displacement).

**Heat morbidity + mortality** — heat is the deadliest weather hazard. **Eric Klinenberg** 'Heat Wave: A Social Autopsy of Disaster in Chicago' (1995) — 1995 Chicago heat wave killed 739 people, concentrated in elderly + isolated + poor + Black neighborhoods (vs adjacent neighborhoods with stronger social cohesion + cooling capacity). Founded modern social-determinants-of-disaster framework. **2003 European heatwave** ~70k excess deaths (Robine 2008 CR Biol). **2010 Russia heatwave** ~55k. Repeated 2022 + 2023 + 2024 Europe + India + Pacific. Each 1 °C above optimal → ~3-5% mortality (Gasparrini 2015 Lancet 384-city study).

**Climate-vector expansion**:
- **Malaria + Anopheles** — temperature-sensitive transmission window; shifting upward in highland East Africa + South America (Caminade + Lowe).
- **Dengue + Aedes aegypti + albopictus** — global range expansion to Europe (France, Italy, Spain), US Southeast, China; >5 million cases/yr (Brady; Bhatt).
- **Lyme + Ixodes scapularis** — northern range expansion in North America + Europe; cases tripled US since 1995 (CDC).
- **Vibrio + warm seas** — bloodstream + wound infections.
- **West Nile, chikungunya, Zika** — periodic outbreaks following vector establishment.

**Food security + climate** — staple crop yields decline ~5-10% per °C warming (Lobell + Schlenker); regional disparities (sub-Saharan Africa most vulnerable). Heat + drought + flooding amplify shocks. Nutritional consequences: micronutrient density of staples falls under elevated CO₂ (Loladze; Smith). FAO + WFP Global Report on Food Crises.

**Climate-driven migration + displacement** — Stern 2007; Black 2011 Nature; IDMC 2024 — ~30 million displaced/yr by climate-related disasters. Trans-border + within-country; intersects with conflict + governance. Health consequences: communicable disease, NCD interruption, mental health, GBV.

**Air pollution-climate co-benefits** — burning fossil fuels causes both PM2.5 deaths + GHG emissions; clean-energy transition delivers immediate health benefits + long-term climate benefits. Health-co-benefits often offset all transition costs (Lelieveld; West; Markandya 2018 Lancet PH).

**Lancet Countdown on Health and Climate Change** — annual indicators tracking exposures, impacts, adaptation, mitigation, finance (Watts; Romanello). 2024 report: record heat exposure (~512 billion person-hours of heat in 2023); $1.6 trillion economic losses; only 27% of countries have national health-adaptation plans.

**IPCC AR6** (2021-23) — Working Group II 'Impacts, Adaptation, Vulnerability' has health chapter (Cissé + Smith 2022); confidence high that climate change is harming health now + will worsen. 1.5 °C target requires net-zero by 2050.

**Planetary health** — concept introduced **Whitmee et al. 2015 Lancet/Rockefeller Foundation 'Safeguarding human health in the Anthropocene'** + **Frank et al.** — health depends on stable Earth systems (climate, biodiversity, freshwater, nutrient cycles, oceans, land use, pollution). Operationalizes Rockström planetary boundaries for health. **Planetary Health Alliance** (Myers, Harvard 2016+) coordinates global research + curriculum. Frames PH as inseparable from Earth-system health.

slides.title: Occupational health + the hierarchy of controls
slides.body:
Occupational health is the original public-health discipline — Ramazzini's 'De Morbis Artificum' (1700) catalogued miners' silicosis + chimney-sweeps' scrotal cancer + lead poisoning in painters centuries before germ theory.

**Classical occupational diseases**:
- **Silicosis** — crystalline silica inhalation (mining, sandblasting, fracking, tunneling, stone-cutting). Engineered-stone silicosis (Australia 2018-23; Hoy + Glass) reached >500 young workers; Australia banned engineered stone 2024. WHO + ILO 'Eliminate Silicosis' by 2030 target.
- **Asbestosis + mesothelioma** — Selikoff 1964 NY insulation cohort + Doll 1955 UK. Latency 20-40 yr; epidemic continues despite bans.
- **Coal worker pneumoconiosis + black lung** — coal-dust inhalation; resurgent in US Appalachia (Blackley + Halldin 2018).
- **Byssinosis** — cotton-dust 'brown lung' in textile mills (Schilling; later replicated in Bangladesh + India).
- **Pesticide poisoning** — organophosphates + paraquat + chlorpyrifos; ~150k unintentional deaths/yr (Eddleston). Rotterdam + Stockholm conventions regulate trade in hazardous chemicals.
- **Heavy-metal poisoning** — lead, mercury, cadmium, arsenic. Minamata 1956+ — methylmercury from Chisso plant in Japan, ~2200 confirmed cases; Minamata Convention 2013.
- **Noise-induced hearing loss** — ~17% of adult hearing loss attributable to work exposure.
- **Musculoskeletal disorders + ergonomics** — repetitive strain, awkward posture, lifting; 30% of work-related illness burden.
- **Heat stress** — agricultural + construction workers in tropics; Gulf migrant labor mortality (Bouchama; Pradhan 2019 BMJ).
- **Occupational cancer** — IARC list: aromatic amines + bladder cancer (dye industry; Case 1954), benzene + leukemia (chemical industry), nickel + chromium + nasal cancer, wood dust + sinonasal, formaldehyde, diesel exhaust.
- **Stress + cardiovascular + mental health** — Karasek + Theorell demand-control model; Marmot Whitehall studies; burnout, PTSD in HCWs.

**Bradford Hill criteria** were developed largely from occupational epidemiology (Doll + Hill 1954 doctors smoking; Selikoff asbestos): his 1965 paper drew explicitly on industrial-exposure causal reasoning.

**The Hawthorne effect** — Western Electric studies 1924-1932 at Hawthorne Works, Chicago. Originally interpreted as showing productivity rose under any change in lighting / conditions because workers knew they were being studied. Re-analyses (Levitt + List 2011) modest. Lesson for occupational + intervention research: blinded + cluster-randomized designs preferred.

**Hierarchy of controls (NIOSH)** — preferred order for hazard mitigation:
1. **Elimination** — remove the hazard entirely (substitute non-toxic material).
2. **Substitution** — replace hazardous material with less hazardous (water-based for solvent paints).
3. **Engineering controls** — physical barriers, ventilation, machine guards, isolation.
4. **Administrative controls** — training, job rotation, work-rest schedules, signage, SOPs.
5. **Personal protective equipment (PPE)** — last resort, weakest control.

**NIOSH HAVAS** — hand-arm vibration syndrome surveillance (vibration-induced white finger in chainsaw + drilling operators).

**Global supply-chain occupational health** — **Rana Plaza (Dhaka, Bangladesh) April 24 2013** — eight-story garment factory collapse killed 1,134 workers + injured 2,500+. Largest industrial accident since Bhopal 1984. Sparked **Accord on Fire and Building Safety in Bangladesh** (2013-2018; IndustriALL + UNI Global + ILO) + Alliance for Bangladesh Worker Safety. Inspections in 1600+ factories; remediation ~85%. Demonstrated weakness of voluntary CSR + need for binding multistakeholder mechanisms in globalized supply chains. Comparable disasters: Tazreen Fashions fire (Bangladesh 2012, 117 dead), Ali Enterprises fire (Karachi 2012, 250+), Triangle Shirtwaist (NY 1911, 146).

**ILO conventions + standards** — fundamental rights (C155 OSH 1981; C170 chemicals; C161 OSH services; C187 promotional framework). National enforcement variable. **WHO Global Plan of Action on Workers' Health 2008-2017** + successor.

**Bhopal 1984** — Union Carbide India Ltd; methyl isocyanate gas leak; ~3800 immediate deaths + ~15-20k total over decade; ~500k injured (Broughton 2005). Inspired chemical-process-safety regimes globally.

question.question: Reasoning about PM2.5 reduction + mortality benefit
question.goal: A city of 5 million has annual PM2.5 of 35 μg/m³ + plans to reduce to 15 μg/m³ over 10 yr via cleaner transport, household-LPG transition, + industrial controls. Estimate health benefits.

steps.prompt: What's the WHO 2021 annual PM2.5 guideline + how far above is the city?
steps.reveal: WHO 2021 AQ guideline: annual PM2.5 ≤ 5 μg/m³. City at 35 → 7× the guideline. Target 15 → 3× guideline (matches WHO Interim Target 3). Aggressive but technically + economically feasible (Beijing reduced PM2.5 ~40% in 5 yr 2013-2017).

steps.prompt: Using the Pope-Dockery concentration-response (~1% all-cause mortality per μg/m³ PM2.5), estimate the per-capita mortality reduction.
steps.reveal: Δ PM2.5 = 20 μg/m³. Pope-Dockery + GBD slopes vary by exposure level, but ~1% all-cause mortality per μg/m³ (or 6-10% per 10 μg/m³ for cardiopulmonary, smaller for all-cause; nonlinear). Rough estimate: 20% reduction in PM2.5-attributable mortality fraction. The IER (Integrated Exposure-Response) of Burnett + Cohen flattens at high levels; benefits are larger closer to the WHO guideline.

steps.prompt: Baseline PM2.5-attributable mortality is ~10% of all-cause; the city has ~40k deaths/yr. How many lives saved/yr after the reduction?
steps.reveal: Baseline PM-attributable deaths = 40,000 × 0.10 = 4,000/yr. Reduce attributable fraction by ~20% → 800 fewer deaths/yr at new steady state. Additional benefits: reduced asthma exacerbations + ED visits + CVD admissions; cognitive + birth-outcome improvements (PM2.5 linked to preterm birth + LBW; Bell).

steps.prompt: What policies achieve the reduction? Map by sector.

acceptedAnswers: transport (EVs + fuel + transit) + household (LPG + electric cooking) + industry (controls + standards) + power (renewables)

steps.reveal: By sector: (a) transport — fleet electrification, low-emission zones (London ULEZ 2019, Madrid Centro, Stockholm), bus+ rail mode-share growth, Euro-6 / Bharat Stage VI standards, retire 2-stroke; (b) household — LPG + electricity (PM Ujjwala India); (c) industry — flue-gas desulfurization, SCR for NOₓ, fugitive-emission controls; (d) power — coal → renewables; (e) agriculture — open-burning bans (Punjab; Indonesia peatlands); (f) construction — dust suppression.

acceptedAnswers: lower-SES + indoor + outdoor exposure overlap; climate co-benefits; just transition for workers

steps.reveal: Equity: lower-SES households face higher indoor (solid-fuel cooking) + outdoor exposure (proximity to roads + industry; Bullard environmental-justice scholarship). Targeted interventions (cookstove subsidies, low-income housing retrofit, clean-bus routes through low-income areas) reduce gradient. Climate co-benefits: fossil-fuel reductions cut both PM2.5 + GHG (Markandya 2018 Lancet PH). Just transition: protect coal + ICE-vehicle workers via retraining + safety net (ILO Just Transition Guidelines 2015).

question.question: Which control sits highest in the NIOSH hierarchy of controls for managing crystalline-silica exposure in stone-cutting?
options: Provide workers with N95 respirators + monthly fit testing.
Substitute engineered stone with low-silica or silica-free alternatives + ban high-silica engineered stone (Australia 2024 model) — eliminating or substituting the hazard at source.
Train workers on the dangers of silica + require quarterly safety briefings.
Increase quarterly low-dose CT screening for silicosis in exposed workers.
question.explanation:
**NIOSH hierarchy of controls**, from most to least effective:
1. **Elimination** — remove the hazard.
2. **Substitution** — replace with less hazardous (engineered-stone ban Australia 2024 is a substitution-via-policy lever).
3. **Engineering controls** — wet cutting, local exhaust ventilation, enclosure.
4. **Administrative controls** — training, job rotation, work-rest schedules.
5. **PPE** — N95 / P100 respirators (last resort + most failure-prone).

Australia's 2018-2023 engineered-stone silicosis outbreak (Hoy + Glass; >500 cases in young workers) followed years of reliance on PPE + administrative controls — which failed. The 2024 nationwide ban on engineered stone (first in the world) is an elimination/substitution control + the most effective intervention. Health screening (option D) is secondary prevention — detects existing disease, doesn't prevent it. PPE + training are the weakest controls. Elimination + substitution have outsized impact + don't depend on worker behavior.

hints: NIOSH ranks elimination + substitution above PPE.
slides.workedSolution: NIOSH hierarchy: elimination > substitution > engineering > administrative > PPE. Banning engineered stone (Australia 2024) is substitution-via-policy + the most effective intervention. PPE + screening are weaker. Australia ban followed >500 young silicosis cases.

question.question: Heat-action plan for a city facing a 45 °C heatwave
question.prompt: Your city of 8 million is forecast to face a 5-day 45 °C heatwave next week; baseline summer heat-mortality ~50/d, expected to triple. Discuss: (a) Klinenberg's 1995 Chicago lessons (social isolation + structural neglect + neighborhood cohesion); (b) early-warning system + thresholds; (c) cooling-centers + outreach to vulnerable groups (elderly alone, homeless, outdoor workers, infants, people on medications); (d) electricity-grid + water-system resilience; (e) hospital + EMS surge planning; (f) communications (multi-lingual, multi-channel); (g) longer-term climate-adaptation (urban greening, cool roofs, building codes, tree canopy equity — Detroit + Phoenix + Ahmedabad heat action plan); (h) intersection with air-quality (heat + ozone), agricultural + construction worker protection (paid heat breaks, hydration), + just transition for outdoor labor; (i) monitoring excess mortality via vital statistics + ED syndromic surveillance.

question.question: A city has PM2.5 annual mean 30 μg/m³ + WHO guideline is 5 μg/m³. Using a ~1% increase in cardiopulmonary mortality per μg/m³ PM2.5 above the guideline (rough linear approximation), what's the approximate cardiopulmonary mortality excess attributable to PM2.5 above guideline?

question.prompt: In ≤120 words, explain why air-pollution control, climate-change mitigation, + occupational safety should be designed together rather than in silos — using PM2.5 + heat + Rana Plaza as worked examples.
question.rubric: Mentions: PM2.5 + GHG share fossil-fuel combustion sources → clean-energy transition delivers immediate health (PM-attributable mortality reduction; Pope-Dockery) + long-term climate co-benefits (Markandya 2018 Lancet PH); climate-change-driven heat increases occupational + general mortality + amplifies vector + food + water risks (Lancet Countdown; Klinenberg); occupational + environmental hazards intersect in global supply chains — Rana Plaza 2013 (1,134 garment-worker deaths) reflects weak labor standards + sourcing pressures + building codes; binding multistakeholder Accord followed. NIOSH hierarchy of controls (elimination + substitution at top, PPE at bottom) applies broadly. Conclude: planetary health (Whitmee + Rockefeller 2015; Frank) reframes environmental + occupational + climate + ecosystem health as a single integrated agenda, with equity at the core.
